sentences.text:
The appellant no.2 - Akaludas Choudhary seeks suspension of sentence in his first attempt in I.A.
No.19565/2024 during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted and sentenced in the following manner :-
 CONVICTION   Section Act Imprisonment Fine if depos  details   302 r/w IPC, 1860 R.I. for life Rs.5,000/-
 34
The appellant no.2 has preferred this application after withdrawal of I.A. No.17801/2024, in which due to some clerical omissions, liberty was granted to the appellant to file a fresh I.A.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the case of the appellant is on parity with that of his wife/appellant no.3 - Ram Kumari, who has already been granted concession of suspension of sentence vide order dated 22.04.2024.

The order dated 22.04.2024 reads as under :-
"Heard on I.A. No.24056/2023, which an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of applicant /appellant No.3 - Ram Kumari, who seeks suspension of sentence 2 CRA-2553-2022 in her third attempt during the pendency of criminal appeal No. 2553 of 2022.
Four persons
were tried in the present case.
All the four persons have been convicted and sentenced to undergo life sentence with fine of Rs. 5000/- each under Section 302/34 of IPC with default stipulations.
Co-convict namely Madan Das @ Lala has already been granted benefit of suspended sentence vide order dated 29.08.2023 passed in Cr.A. No. 5466 of 2023.
Co-convict Bhajan Das is the husband of deceased Neetu Choudhary.
The cause of death as per medical opinion is stated to be strangulation.
The appellant along with other co-convicts have been tried for the offence under Section 304B /34 IPC, 498A, 302 IPC and under section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

The factum of death having Bhajandas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175488168/
1 been caused within a period 7 years could not be proved and therefore, the appellant and other co-convicts have been acquitted for the offences under Section 304B/34 of IPC.

sentences.text:
Similarly, demand of dowry and cruelty could not be established and therefore,
appellant and other co-convicts have also been acquitted for the offences under Section 498A IPC and under section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The appellant Ramkumari has been convicted with the aid of Section 34 under Section 302 IPC on the ground of her presence in the house.
Her husband Akalu Das Choudhary has also been convicted and sentenced accordingly.

Prima facie, it can be appreciated that there is no eyewitness account in the present case except a presumption arising out of the presence of the appellant / applicant in the matrimonial house in which death of deceased Neetu Choudhary has taken place.
Husband of the deceased namely Bhajan Das is in custody.
Husband of the present appellant namely Akalu Das is also in custody.
The appellant being a lady can be considered for grant of suspension of sentence at this stage.

The complicity of appellant/applicant would remain debatable in the absence of eyewitness account and particularly in view of her acquittal for the offences under Section 304B/34, 498A of IPC and under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The present appellant has undergone more than 2 years and 3 months of actual sentence as on date.

Plea of learned State counsel in respect of presumption regarding presence of the applicant in the matrimonial house, where murder has taken place, would remain debatable and would be subject to appreciation of 3 CRA-2553-2022 material collected by the police at the time of final disposal of the case.

In view of aforesaid, we deem it appropriate to direct the release of the applicant/appellant No.3-Ram Kumari, by suspending her remaining jail sentence,
subject to her executing adequate bail bond and surety bond to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned with a further direction to appear before the trial Court concerned on 12.08.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, during the pendency of this appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No.24056/2023 is allowed.
Nothing observed herein above shall be construed to be an opinion on the merits of the case.
Certified copy as per rules."
Evidently, Ramkumari and the present appellant have been convicted with the aid of Section 34 I.P.C. for the offence under Section 302 I.P.C. on the ground of their presence in the house.
There was no eye-witness in the present case except for the presumption drawn against the appellants due to their presence in the matrimonial house in which the death of Neetu Singh took place.
The husband of Neetu Singh namely Bhajan Das/appellant no.1 is in custody.
The present appellant has also undergone more than 4 years of actual sentence as on date.
Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant.
However, the factum of the order dated 22.04.2024 could not be denied.

sentences.text:
For the reasons recorded in the aforesaid order dated 22.04.2024, the 4 CRA-2553-2022 present appellant no.2 - Akaludas Choudhary is also granted indulgence of this Court by suspending his jail sentence, subject to his executing bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only)
and one surety bond in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned, with a further direction to appear before the trial Court concerned on 24.10.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, during the pendency of this appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No.19565/2024 is allowed.
Certified copy as per rules.
(RAJ MOHAN SINGH)

(DEVNARAYAN  JUDGE JUDG  Priya.P Bhajandas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175488168/
